author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: I am pushing for the acceptance criteria to be fully automated so that model evaluation starts immediately when the conditions are met. Right now, the process relies on manual checks, which introduces delays and human error. I want the system to trigger the evaluation workflow the moment the criteria are satisfied, without waiting for a person to manually initiate it. This ensures we catch performance issues faster and keep the deployment pipeline moving smoothly. The more automated this step is, the better it is for maintaining consistent reliability across our services. I am not asking for a new tool, just for the existing logic to be wired up so it runs itself. This will help us iterate on the models more effectively and reduce the time between a change and its validation.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that increasing the level of automation makes the system better for maintaining consistent reliability, indicating that doing more than the minimum requested (full automation) would make them happier.
